title: Titan: A Golden Case in Indian Retail - [Business Breakdowns, EP. 105]
thesis: The episode argues that TITAN is a strong investment driven by significant growth potential in its wedding jewelry, sari, and diaspora segments, which could support extended revenue growth and high free cash flow compounding. However, this bullish view is tempered by bearish concerns regarding the watches business, which faces a stagnated industry and demographic headwinds from mobile phones, making future growth in that segment uncertain.

claims.claim: The speaker believes TITAN can achieve 13-14% revenue growth for an extended period due to drivers in the wedding market, the rise of Indian women in the workforce, and the diaspora.
claims.quote: you're looking at a business where we reckon revenue growth at the 13 14% level should be doable for an extended period of time

claims.claim: The speaker expects TITAN to compound free cash flow at 25% by improving efficiencies and squeezing inventory days.
claims.quote: keep your efficiencies going using the sorts of tech innovations we discussed bad compounding around the 20% mark and then free cash look compounding at the 25% mark by squeezing inventory days even further

claims.claim: The speaker views TITAN's Sari business as a significant growth opportunity, noting it is a 20 billion dollar market ripe for disruption.
claims.quote: twenty billion dollar business at its infancy we reckon this could also be part of the juice up on that 25% free cash look compounding

claims.claim: The speaker worries about the watches business, stating it is difficult to see how it will grow given the rise of mobile phones and a young demographic.
claims.quote: again young country 28 median age I'm not so sure how many youngsters will buy this so this part of the business I think will struggle to grow

claims.claim: The speaker expresses concern that the watches business is struggling due to a stagnated industry, despite TITAN's past growth.
claims.quote: this is the part of the business which is struggling not for any fault of titan it's struggling because watches in the industries is a industry which is stagnated

claims.claim: The speaker notes that while TITAN has grown watches revenue at 10% over the last decade, the industry is stagnated and future growth is uncertain.
